questions.text: Which floor-plan requirement is directly supported by checked PD 1096?

options.text: Floor plans must be drawn to scale not less than 1:100 and show gridlines plus complete room or functional-space identification.
Floor plans must always be drawn at 1:20.
Floor plans need only furniture symbols.
Floor plans are not part of architectural documents.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 lists floor plans among architectural documents and states the minimum scale and identification requirements.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Rule VIII Section 808 (Door Widths); BP 344 2024 IRR Section 4.5BP 344 2024 IRR (Accessible Door Width—0.85m minimum)

questions.text: Which accessible elements does checked PD 1096 require as details in architectural documents?

options.text: Accessible ramps, stairs, lifts/elevators, entrances, corridors, and walkways.
Only decorative landscaping.
Only kitchen counters.
Only furniture schedules.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 lists details for accessible ramps, accessible stairs, accessible lifts/elevators, accessible entrances, corridors, and walkways.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 Section 505 (Plans—Fire-Rated Assembly Notation); PHILGBC/AIA Standards

questions.text: What accessibility document requirement is source-safe under PD 1096?

options.text: Plans and specific locations of all accessibility facilities at scale of at least 1:100.
A verbal note with no drawing location.
Only a perspective view.
No accessibility plan is required.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 requires plans and specific locations of all accessibility facilities at a stated scale.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); PD 1096 Section 505 (Plans & Specifications—Dimensioning)

questions.text: Which fire-safety content is source-safe for plan documentation?

options.text: A floor layout indicating evacuation route, emergency lights, signs, fire exits, and related fire-safety items.
Only furniture color schedules.
Only structural rebar sizes.
No fire-safety information is shown on plans.

questions.rationale: PD 1096 requires fire-safety documents including layout plans with evacuation routes and fire-safety devices.
questions.code_citation: BP 344 (Accessibility Law); PD 1096 Section 505 (Plans showing accessible features)

questions.text: Which checked BP 344 definition helps test floor-plan accessibility?

options.text: Accessible route as a continuous unobstructed path connecting accessible elements and spaces.
Accessible route as any stair-only path.
Accessible route as only a driveway.
Accessible route as a decorative arrow.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 defines accessible route as continuous and unobstructed, connecting accessible elements and spaces safely and independently.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); AIA Graphic Standards

questions.text: Which door clear width is supported by the checked BP 344 2024 source for the cited accessible room condition?

options.text: At least 900 mm clear width.
At least 600 mm clear width.
Exactly 1200 mm for every door.
No clear width is stated.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 source states the cited room doorway shall have a clear width of at least 900 mm.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards)

questions.text: Which accessible parking information is source-safe to show or coordinate on plans?

options.text: Accessible parking slot count, location near accessible entrances, minimum 4000 mm by 5000 mm size, and required signage.
Only a generic P label with no route or dimensions.
Accessible parking in ramped or sloping areas.
No accessible parking information.

questions.rationale: The checked BP 344 parking text covers slot count, location, dimensions, and signage.

questions.text: Which source-safe floor-plan approach avoids overclaiming?

options.text: Show the accessible element and cite the checked requirement that controls it.
Apply a remembered drafting convention as if it were law.
Use RA 7277 text not raw-audited in this batch.
Treat all dimensions as interior clear widths without source support.

questions.rationale: Batch 066 floor-plan edits are limited to checked PD 1096 and BP 344 requirements.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); AIA (American Institute of Architects) Graphic Standards

questions.text: Which BP 344 signage element can be coordinated on a floor plan?

options.text: Directional signs using the International Symbol of Access to lead to facilities such as elevators, entrances, toilets, and parking.
Only restaurant menu boards.
Only structural grid bubbles.
No accessibility signage.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 requires directional signs incorporating the International Symbol of Access at passageways and changes in direction.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); PD 1096 Section 505 (Plans—Dimensioning & Notation)

questions.text: Which source-safe statement applies to areas of refuge on plans?

options.text: They are fire-separated areas with direct access to an exit where persons unable to use stairs may temporarily await assistance.
They are storage closets with no exit relation.
They replace all required exits.
They are only parking stalls.

questions.rationale: BP 344 2024 defines an area of refuge with direct access to an exit and fire separation for temporary safety.
questions.code_citation: ISO 1091 (Architectural Graphic Standards); AIA Graphic Standards
